messages:
SRE-Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: inference-prod-gpu pool at 100% alloc, queue length=1200, autoscaler reports maxNodes reached (40). Paging @oncall and eng-sre. See metrics: https://dash.redwood.io/d/inf-prod/gpu-pool?from=now-1h
Jason: Oncall ack. I'm pulling `kubectl get pods -n inference` now — lots of Pending with `Insufficient GPUs`.
Priya: Confirming — 72 Pending pods, most request 4 GPUs. Node logs show `scaleUp forbidden: reached max size` from cluster-autoscaler.
Mark: CA config shows `maxNodes: 40` for inference-prod-asg. Looks like we've hit the ceiling.
Jason: Can we do a manual bump of the ASG desired/desired? What's the approved escalation path for immediate customers?
Liam: I can execute a manual ASG increase but need scope approval. Which customers are affected and what's the impact?
Sophie: Support: Customer `beta-market` (tier: paid-enterprise) reported widespread 502s and timeouts (ticket #4567). SLA breach alerts firing.
Jason: OK plan: (1) bump ASG desired to +10 nodes (to 50) to absorb backlog, (2) update CA `maxNodes` to >= 60 so autoscaler can continue, (3) monitor scheduling and queue. Priya, can you verify taints/labels that might block scheduling?
Priya: Running checks: ```
kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep Pending
kubectl describe pod <one-pending-pod>
```  Most Pending reason: `Insufficient GPUs`. Also see intermittent `node(s) had taint {gpu=true:NoSchedule}` on burst pool nodes.
Cameron: If we temporarily remove the taint on the burst pool nodes they can accept GPU workloads: ```
kubectl taint nodes <burst-node-name> gpu=true:NoSchedule-  # trailing dash removes taint
```  Would need coordination — these nodes normally host non-ML infra.
Mark: I'll increase the ASG desired capacity now. Running: ```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name inference-prod-asg --desired-capacity 50 --honor-cooldown
```  Kicking it off.
SRE-Bot: Deploy-bot: ASG update started for inference-prod-asg; requested capacity 50.
Jason: New nodes are provisioning. Seeing kubelet join events. Pods scheduling — queue dropping from 1200 -> ~480 in the last 8m. Latency for critical endpoints down from 2.8s -> 1.1s (P95).
Sophie: Customer `beta-market` status: errors significantly reduced. I'll send an interim update: "We're mitigating, scaling cluster to relieve queue; follow-up once stable."
Liam: Updated CA config: bumped `maxNodes` 40 -> 70 so CA can autoscale instead of manual touches. Also enabled a short-lived burst policy for this pool in infra to prevent immediate re-hit.
Priya: KV cache warmups are ongoing; some cold-start latency still expected but overall throughput improving. Monitoring for any OOMs or scheduling failures.
Jason: Handing off monitoring & stabilization to Mark for the next hour. I'll create the incident doc and start timeline. Please add any actions in thread. :thumbsup:
Mark: Action items so far: [1] Add early-warning alert when CA hits >= 90% of maxNodes, [2] Document emergency ASG bump steps in runbook, [3] Review taint usage on burst pool and consider a dedicated untainted overflow pool, [4] Postmortem to include thresholds for per-customer backpressure.
Cameron: +1 on dedicated overflow pool. Also propose a safety margin in CA configs (maxNodes = steady + 50% buffer) for high-variance workloads.
SRE-Bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: inference-prod-gpu backlog cleared, queue < 50, autoscaler can manage growth. Incident duration ~32m. Incident ticket created INC-2026-789.
